question: 1 { kJ} = {______ J}
solution:
The correct answer is __**1000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The unit **kJ** represents a **kilojoule**, which is a multiple of the base unit of energy, the **joule (J)**.
 
• In the **International System of Units (SI)**, the prefix **kilo-** is used to denote a factor of **10³** or **1000**.
 
• The **joule** is defined as the amount of **energy transferred** to an object when a force of **one newton** acts on that object in the direction of the force's motion through a distance of **one meter**.
 
• Mathematically, the relationship is defined as **1 kilojoule = 1000 joules**. This conversion is fundamental in **thermodynamics**, **physics**, and **chemistry** when measuring heat or work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metric System Multiples**:

 
 
• **Mega (M)**: Represents **10⁶** or **1,000,000** units. Therefore, **1 MJ = 1,000,000 J**.
 
• **Giga (G)**: Represents **10⁹** or **1,000,000,000** units.
 
• **Milli (m)**: Represents **10−³** or **1/1000** of a unit. Therefore, **1 mJ = 0.001 J**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• The unit is named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**, who demonstrated the **mechanical equivalent of heat** in the **19th century**.
 
 
 
• **Energy Conversions**:
 
 
• **1 calorie (cal)** is equivalent to approximately **4.184 joules**.
 
• **1 kilowatt-hour (kWh)**, often used for electrical energy billing, is equal to **3,600,000 joules** or **3600 kJ**.
 
• The **joule** can also be expressed in terms of other SI units as **1 kg·m²/s²** or **1 Watt-second**.
